title: A plugin guard
description:
Build `PluginGuard`, through which the game calls every plugin.

- `call(plugin, fn)` calls `fn` (a `std::function<void()>`) for the named plugin, unless that plugin is disabled. If `fn` throws any exception, the guard catches it, records one failure for the plugin together with the exception's message (`what()` for `std::exception`, `"unknown error"` otherwise), and returns `false`. A successful call returns `true`; a call to a disabled plugin returns `false` without running `fn`.
- After `maxFailures` failures (given to the constructor) a plugin is **disabled** for the rest of the session.
- `disabled(plugin)` says whether it is disabled; `failures(plugin)` how many failures it has; `lastError(plugin)` the last recorded message (empty if none).
- `report()` lists, alphabetically, a line for every plugin with at least one failure: `"name: N failure(s), last: MESSAGE"`, followed by `" (disabled)"` if it is disabled.
hints: Keep a `std::map` from plugin name to its failure count and last message. `call` checks `disabled` first, then runs `fn` inside `try`.
Catch `const std::exception&` first, to use `what()`, then `...` for anything else.
lessonTitle: Architecture: Keeping Mods Modular and Stable
